exposure: antenatal findings (normal USG, fetal growth restriction, abruptio placenta)
outcome: neonatal hypoxic and ischemic brain injuries
blood flow irregularities (resistive index, peak systolic velocity)
sensitivity and specificity of USG for detecting PVL
cohort: The study included 116 neonates with birth asphyxia or suspected hypoxic-ischemic injury, 50.43% of whom were preterm.
finding: The study found that USG findings correlated significantly with lower APGAR scores, particularly for Periventricular Leukomalacia (PVL), demonstrating high sensitivity for early PVL detection and moderate specificity compared to MRI.
mod_finding: Mode of delivery significantly influenced the risk of neonatal hypoxic-ischemic injuries.
